intro: Every profile leaves the plant finished. Anodising and powder coating run on our own lines in Binh Duong, so colour is a production step rather than a subcontract, and a repeat order two years later still matches.

items.name: Natural Silver
items.note: The reference anodised finish. 15 µm on exterior work, 10 µm inside.

items.name: Champagne
items.note: Electrolytically coloured, not dyed, so the tone does not drift under UV.

items.name: Light Bronze
items.note: The most specified bronze on facade work in this region.

items.name: Dark Bronze
items.note: Deep bronze. Batch control matters here; we hold ±2 ΔE across a run.

items.name: Anodic Black
items.note: Two-step black. Fingerprints show less than on black powder.

items.name: Pale Gold
items.note: Interior trim and shopfitting. Not recommended on coastal exteriors.

items.name: Brushed Silver
items.note: Linear brush before anodising. Grain direction is specified per elevation.

items.name: Marine Silver
items.note: 25 µm anodic layer for coastal and offshore exposure.

items.name: Traffic White
items.note: The volume white. Held in stock, no minimum batch.

items.name: Pure White
items.note: Slightly warmer than 9016. Common on interior joinery.

items.name: White Aluminium
items.note: Metallic grey. Reads close to natural anodised at a distance.

items.name: Grey Aluminium
items.note: Darker metallic. Pairs with dark bronze on mixed elevations.

items.name: Anthracite Grey
items.note: The default dark grey on residential window systems.

items.name: Black Grey
items.note: Reads black in daylight without the heat gain of true black.

items.name: Jet Black
items.note: Surface temperature runs high in direct sun; check thermal break sizing.

items.name: Chocolate Brown
items.note: Long-standing choice on villa joinery.

items.name: Moss Green
items.note: Heritage and conservation work.

items.name: Gentian Blue
items.note: Industrial and institutional. Strong colour retention.

items.name: Traffic Red
items.note: Signage, retail fronts and plant rooms.

items.name: Oyster White
items.note: Warm off-white for interior partitions.

items.name: Quartz Grey
items.note: Fine texture hides handling marks on site.

items.name: Sablé Bronze
items.note: Coarse texture. The usual answer when a facade must not show installation scuffs.

items.name: Light Oak
items.note: Sublimated over a powder base. Grain runs along the extrusion.

items.name: Walnut
items.note: The most requested wood tone on sliding systems.

items.name: Burma Teak
items.note: Warmer and redder than walnut.

items.name: Grey Ash
items.note: Weathered timber look without the maintenance.

items.name: Wenge
items.note: Dark interior joinery and shopfitting.

items.name: PVDF Metallic Silver
items.note: Two-coat PVDF. Specified where a 20-year colour warranty is required.

items.name: PVDF Storm Grey
items.note: Three-coat option available for high-UV sites.

items.name: PVDF Bronze
items.note: Matches AN-320 closely enough to mix anodised and coated on one elevation.

items.name: PVDF Champagne
items.note: Where champagne is wanted on a coated rather than anodised substrate.

items.name: PVDF Marine White
items.note: Salt-spray tested to 4,000 hours.

items.name: Mirror Polish
items.note: Polished then clear-anodised. Interior feature work only.

items.name: Sandblasted
items.note: Even matt surface that takes fingerprints far less readily than polish.

items.name: Hairline
items.note: Fine unidirectional grain, standard on handles and trims.
